newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Colonial calls for mega-regulator.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Colonial calls for mega-regulator.

text.p: Australian life office Colonial Mutual called on Monday for a "super regulator" to supervise the entire financial services industry, including insurers, banks and fund managers.

"The convergence of the financial services industry means it is important a single prudential regulator oversees the total industry," Colonial Mutual group managing director Peter Smedley said in a statement.
Outlining its submission to the official Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system, Smedley also advocated the creation of a single consumer-protection watchdog.
Colonial said the Australian Securities Commission should take responsibility for consumer protection and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission should focus on competition policy only.
"In the end, consumers bear the costs of overly complex regulation," Smedley said in support of what he called a "twin peaks" regulatory framework.
Colonial's submission is similar to a call from rival life office National Mutual Holdings Ltd for a super regulator to provide prudental supervision.
The Reserve Bank of Australia has opposed the notion of a super regulator.
The central bank argues that banks deserve special attention because, as holders of short-term liabilities and long-term assets, they are especially vulnerable to runs on funds.
Colonial Mutual said it was in a unique position to comment because, as owner of the State Bank of New South Wales, the group was involved in banking, insurance and funds management.
The Wallis inquiry, headed by former paper industry executive Stan Wallis, is to issue a discussion paper at the end of November and make its final recommendations in March.
Colonial's Smedley said changes ushered in by the Wallis inquiry must be simple, pragmatic and efficient and should not take a world-leadership approach for the sake of it.
"We have to look beyond pure market theory or ideology to make sure that our regulatory environment allows us to compete on equal terms internationally," he said.
